# Quotation marks

> **这页管什么**：一律用直引号；标点放引号里还是外。
>
> 来源：<https://developers.google.com/style/quotation-marks> · CC BY 4.0 · 本文件是**规则摘要**，非原文全文。

## Straight vs curly

**Always use straight quotation marks and straight apostrophes.** Curly (typographic) marks are discouraged.

Reasons: code syntax needs straight marks, so consistency simplifies writing; both automated conversion and manual typing of curly marks are error-prone; distinguishing the two makes proofreading harder.

## When to use quotation marks

Sparingly, mainly for:

- Titles of shorter works (articles, web series episodes), unless part of a link.
- Referring to a section of a document when direct linking isn't possible.
- Referring to a parent document's title when already linking to a specific section.
- Directly citing a person's words, or quoting a slogan or motto.
- Using a term in a non-standard, metaphorical way not established in the domain.

Full-length works use *italics* instead.

## Punctuation placement

Commas and periods go **inside** quotation marks.

**Exception**: when quoting a keyword or exact literal string, punctuation goes **outside**, because the quotation marks indicate an exact literal. The preferred approach is to avoid quotation marks around code-font items entirely and use code formatting.

## Single quotation marks

Two approved uses only: in code examples for languages that use them, and for nesting a quote inside another quote (outer double, inner single).
